subject: physical-education
unitTitle: Safety, Self-Care, and Knowing When to Stop
title: Concept model A: distinguishing training discomfort from warning pain
focus: distinguishing training discomfort from warning pain
essentialQuestion: What does taking care of myself look like when no one is telling me to?
privacySafeScenario: Write the self-care and stop-rule protocol the learner will actually run as an adult, including the specific conditions under which they will stop, rest, or seek professional care.
studentTask: Learner applies distinguishing training discomfort from warning pain in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind distinguishing training discomfort from warning pain and name one adjustment for the next session.
completionCriteria: The learner completes or fully describes the distinguishing training discomfort from warning pain task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
adaptationChoices: The protocol may be written, tabled, or described; a learner managing an ongoing condition builds it with guardian input around constraints they already have.
extensionChallenge: Apply distinguishing training discomfort from warning pain under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The protocol may be written, tabled, or described; a learner managing an ongoing condition builds it with guardian input around constraints they already have.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of distinguishing training discomfort from warning pain in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
